observation.visible_scene: A slow-motion, side-on view of a dark teal water surface against a plain white background, with a bright cyan underwater region below the surface line. A single wave crest rises near the center of the frame, topped by a small rounded protrusion, and several dark air bubbles are suspended in the cyan water beneath the surface (one isolated bubble on the left and a small cluster near the center-bottom).
visible_changes: The central crest's top protrusion progressively deforms: it elongates and curls forward and downward, developing into a hook-like lip with an enclosed cavity/air pocket beneath it by the middle and later frames; the crest body thickens and its silhouette continuously reshapes rather than translating.
The surface line to the left of the crest undulates and lowers slightly over the excerpt, while the crest itself remains roughly centered horizontally.
The suspended bubbles drift slowly rightward relative to the wave crest and subtly change shape (some elongate/flatten), but all bubbles remain present throughout with no merging or disappearance.
The overall water color scheme (dark teal above, bright cyan below, white sky) and the number of visible bubbles persist as stable properties across the clip.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or prior state of the crest's curling motion is not shown; the deformation is already underway at the first frame and continues past the last.
Whether the wave would break, collapse, or settle after this excerpt is unseen.
What produced the submerged bubbles or their motion is not visible.
uncertain_details: The background is featureless, so it cannot be determined whether the bubbles' rightward shift relative to the crest reflects bubble motion, camera panning, or both; the crest's near-constant horizontal position argues against a simple global camera pan.
Exact vertical height change of the crest is small and within noise of deformation; no clear rise/fall trend can be confirmed beyond the shape change.
